intro: This is the Mona Lisa by Leonardo da Vinci.

year: It was painted in the early 1500s.
technique: Da Vinci used sfumato, a soft blending technique.
features: The subtle smile and calm gaze are its most famous features.
history: It became one of the most recognized paintings in the world.
extra: Many visitors are surprised by how small it is in person.

year: It was painted in the early 1500s during the High Renaissance.
technique: Da Vinci used sfumato, layering thin glazes to blur hard edges and create lifelike transitions.
features: Her expression appears to shift as you move, partly due to how the eyes and mouth are modeled.
history: Over time, this portrait became a global icon of portrait painting and museum culture.
extra: Engineers often appreciate da Vinci for combining artistic practice with technical observation.

intro: This is The Starry Night by Vincent van Gogh.

technique: The thick brushwork creates visible movement.
features: The swirling sky and bright stars dominate the scene.
history: It became a symbol of emotional expression in modern art.
extra: People often connect with its energy even without knowing its history.

year: Van Gogh painted it in 1889 while living in Saint-Remy.
technique: He used impasto, building paint thickness so strokes carry direction and rhythm.
features: The cypress, village, and sky are organized to balance calm structure with emotional motion.
history: The work later became central to how people understand expressive modern painting.
extra: Its color contrasts are deliberate, using cool blues against intense yellows to amplify impact.

intro: This is The Last Supper by Leonardo da Vinci.

year: It was created in the late 1400s.
features: All lines pull your focus toward the center.
history: It became one of the most studied religious artworks.
extra: You can read the apostles as a sequence of emotional reactions.

year: Da Vinci worked on it around 1495 to 1498.
technique: He structured the room with one-point perspective so architectural lines converge near Christ.
features: The apostles are grouped in dynamic clusters, each reacting differently to the central moment.
history: Its composition strongly influenced later narrative painting in Europe.
extra: Even non-religious viewers often notice how cinematic the staging feels.

intro: This is Girl with a Pearl Earring by Johannes Vermeer.

features: The direct gaze and pearl highlight create intimacy.
history: It is often called the Mona Lisa of the North.
extra: Its simple background keeps your focus on expression.

year: Vermeer painted it in the Dutch Golden Age, likely in the 1660s.
technique: He used subtle value shifts and controlled highlights to model skin and fabric with precision.
features: The turned pose, parted lips, and bright pearl create a feeling of immediate presence.
history: The painting later became a touchstone for studies of light and portrait intimacy.
extra: Its minimal setting is a design choice that amplifies visual focus.

intro: This is The Persistence of Memory by Salvador Dali.

technique: He rendered dream imagery with precise realism.
features: The melting clocks are the painting's best known feature.
history: It became a defining image of surrealism.
extra: Many visitors read it as a challenge to rigid schedules and certainty.

year: Dali painted it in 1931 during a key phase of surrealism.
technique: He used polished, almost photographic painting methods to depict irrational dream logic.
features: Soft clocks drape over hard surfaces, contrasting precision with instability.
history: The image became one of the most recognizable symbols of surrealist thought.
extra: Its tension between order and distortion makes it relatable to both artists and engineers.
